question: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

On 11 May 2026, units of the Libyan coastguard opened fire on the civilian rescue vessel ‘Sea-Watch 5’ – which had just performed a rescue operation in international waters – and threatened to tow it to Libya. The incident occurred despite earlier assurances from the Commission that it had stepped up monitoring and dialogue mechanisms in the wake of the attack on the rescue vessel ‘Ocean Viking’ in August 2025. Reports of severe violence against migrants in Libya at the hands of civilian, state and quasi-state actors are currently on the rise. 1.

Under which framework (EU-funded programmes, cooperation frameworks or EUbacked bilateral agreements) did the EU supply, retrofit, maintain, co-finance or otherwise support the vessels involved in the incident (patrol boats 101, 662 ‘Murzuq’ and 648 ‘Ras Jadir’)?

What specific steps has the Commission taken since the attack on the ‘Ocean Viking’ in August 2025 to bolster its monitoring and dialogue mechanisms with the Libyan authorities, what incidents have been dealt with and what consequences ensued?

What criteria does the Commission use to decide whether incidents warrant the suspension, cutting or discontinuation of EU funding, training, equipment support or operational cooperation, and does it consider the aforementioned incident to be an escalation that necessitates changes to the current approach?
